newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed higher on Tuesday, getting a leg up from a surprising decline in the September National Association of Purchasing Managers (NAPM) index of U.S. manufacturing activity, dealers said.
The NAPM index dropped to 51.7 in September, versus a forecast 52.5, boosting U.S. and European bond markets. In August the index stood at 52.6.
Amsterdam dealers said the stronger tone could continue with plenty of interested investors still on the sidelines.
"There is still real buying interest bubbling under in the market," one said.
Traders said the combination of lots of money on the sidelines looking for the right time to get into the market with tightening supplies of paper might soon start squeezing prices higher.
"A lot of investors are behind schedule with where they want their portfolios to be," one said.
"As long as no big figure comes out too strong we still have a very, very favourable environment for bonds."
U.S. September payrolls figures are due on Friday and will likely prove the focus for the rest of the week, dealers said. -- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040
